messages:
maria: Heads-up — the micro-econ sentinel dashboard is showing negative per-invocation savings for tenant `acme-inc` after we flipped prefetched-path. Small tenant, low sample rate, and routing fallbacks involved. screenshot pasted in thread.
jakob: I saw that too. Negative savings usually means we double-counted credits or didn't upscale sampled rows. :thinking_face:
tara: Can you paste the pipeline/query that produced the numbers? I want to check the sampling logic and whether fallbacks are excluded.
maria: sure — extracted the aggregation we run for the card:
```
SELECT tenant_id,
       SUM(token_cost) AS total_cost,
       SUM(prefetch_credit) AS credits,
       SUM(token_cost) - SUM(prefetch_credit) AS net_cost
FROM invocation_sample
WHERE sample = true AND day = '2026-03-18'
GROUP BY tenant_id
```
kyle: ah — there it is. Using sample = true without scaling up by 1/sample_rate will make credits appear too small relative to cost. if credits were only logged on prefetched requests, net_cost can go negative once you upscale only one side. we should compute weighted sums like SUM(value / sample_rate).
jakob: additionally, the UI rollup applies a "fallback multiplier" for routing cost to reflect cross-model proxies. I think that multiplier is applied after the DB aggregation, so when we upscale we multiply again — double-scaling.
sophie: repro steps I used: enable prefetched-path for a route on staging, set sample_rate=0.1, run 1k warmups, then 50 actual tiny invokes. dashboard showed -$0.12 savings per invocation for the tenant.
tara: two actionable bugs then: (1) aggregation must use weighted sums for sampled rows; (2) UI shouldn't re-apply fallback multipliers on already adjusted figures. I'll propose a fix split across backend and frontend.
maria: UX note — can we also surface a small "sampling confidence" pill on the card? People keep assuming sampled numbers are exact. Something like: "Estimated (10% sample) ±15%".
kyle: yes, and maybe show a toggle to view scaled vs raw numbers so infra folks can debug easily. :gear:
jakob: for the backend change I'm thinking: alter the ETL job to output both raw_sample_count and scaled_total (value / sample_rate), plus a provenance field describing whether credit came from prefetch, hotpath, or fallback. that makes UI decisions simpler.
tara: I'll open a PR for the ETL: add scaled_token_cost, scaled_prefetch_credit, sample_rate, and credit_source enum. Also add a regression test with synthetic small-tenant traffic to catch negative-savings cases.
devops-bot: deploy-checklist created: https://ci.internal/changes/PR-3893 — run integration tests, check cost-card delta < 1% for large tenants, flag small-tenant variance > 30%.
sophie: quick UX question — should we hide per-invocation sparklines for tenants under X invocations/day? noisy ones make support tickets.
maria: I think hide by default but add an "override" with a warning tooltip. we want to avoid misleading precision.
tara: decision: backend change + UI badge + hide-low-volume sparklines. I'll assign tasks:
- tara: backend ETL PR (adds scaled fields + provenance) — PR 3893
- jakob: frontend change to stop double-multiplying and surface sample_rate/confidence — PR 3894
- kyle: add regression test harness and sampling sim — PR 3895
- sophie: small-tenant UX copy + tooltip — PR 3896
maria: thanks all. Can someone add a short note in the rollout checklist to watch the sentinel alerts for 24h after deploy? I don't want a surprise spike in reported savings.
devops-bot: noted. alert rule created: econ-sentinel/sampled-negative-savings (> 5 tenants) — quiet window 1h.
jakob: I'll pair with tara on the ETL tests tomorrow. if we can ship this before Friday that'd be ideal.
maria: perfect. tagging @eng-oncall FYI. :thumbsup:
